options.summary: Set the destination group from the source
options.detail: Also spelled -g. An unprivileged receiver can preserve only groups it belongs to. Names usually map across the peers. --numeric-ids preserves group numbers directly.

options.detail: The receiver normally needs superuser privileges to create nodes. This preserves their identities. --copy-devices reads the contents of the sending device as a regular file.

options.summary: Read a source device as file data
options.detail: The sender reads the device contents. The receiver can write a regular file, or a device when --write-devices is enabled. A daemon refuses this option by default.

options.summary: Write file data into destination devices
options.detail: Implies --inplace. Existing device contents can be overwritten and an interruption leaves a partial update. A daemon refuses this option by default.

options.summary: Recreate special files on the receiver
options.detail: Includes FIFOs and named sockets. These normally require no superuser privilege. Use --devices for character and block devices. -D requests both kinds.

options.summary: Refuse device and special-file creation on the receiver
options.detail: Upstream 3.5.2 supports this option. Both reviewed Ubuntu releases reject it. Existing nodes remain. Unlike --no-D, this keeps the file-list encoding compatible when set on only one end. A plain switch on a push affects the local sender only. Use -M--drop-D for a supporting remote receiver.

options.summary: Preserve devices and special files
options.detail: Combines --devices and --specials. The receiver normally needs privileges to recreate device nodes. Included by --archive. Use --no-D after -a to disable both.

options.summary: Preserve source modification times
options.detail: Also spelled -t. Lets later runs skip unchanged files by size and modification time. Applies to directories and symlinks too unless --omit-dir-times or --omit-link-times is set.

options.summary: Preserve source access times
options.detail: Also spelled -U. Repeat -U to also request --open-noatime, so reading a file is less likely to alter its access time during the copy.

options.summary: Open files without updating access time
options.detail: Uses O_NOATIME on platforms that support it. Filesystem mount settings may already suppress access-time updates.

options.summary: Preserve file creation times
options.detail: Also spelled -N. Requires a build and receiving filesystem that can set creation times. Both reviewed Ubuntu clients list the option in help, report no crtimes in --version and reject -N.

options.summary: Skip setting directory timestamps
options.detail: Also spelled -O. Skips modification, access and creation times for directory entries. Implied by --backup without --backup-dir. Also prevents early creation of missing directories during incremental recursion.

options.summary: Skip setting symlink timestamps
options.detail: Also spelled -J. Skips modification, access and creation times for symlink entries. Requested timestamps on other file types are still preserved.

options.summary: Attempt privileged metadata operations on the receiver
options.detail: Makes rsync attempt operations such as setting owner or creating device nodes even under a non-root identity. It grants no privileges. Failed operations can then report errors. Overrides --fake-super.

options.summary: Omit preservation of group ownership

options.summary: Begin copying before the recursive scan finishes
options.detail: Also spelled --i-r. With -r and peers at least 3.0.0, incremental recursion is normally automatic and reduces memory use. Options needing a complete list, including --delete-before, --delete-after, --delay-updates and --prune-empty-dirs, disable it.

options.summary: Scan the complete tree before transferring
options.detail: Also spelled --no-i-r. Uses the older full file list with recursion. This delays the first transfer and can increase memory use. It also makes the total file count available before progress starts.

options.summary: Keep the source path below the destination
options.detail: Also spelled -R. For /data/site/img.png the receiver creates data/site/img.png below the destination. Write /data/./site/img.png to keep only site/img.png. Intermediate path components are implied directories, even when they are symlinks on the sender.

options.summary: Keep existing intermediate destination paths
options.detail: Also spelled --no-i-d. With --relative, create missing intermediate directories with default attributes. Existing components keep their attributes and can remain symlinks to directories.

options.summary: Include directories without a recursive walk
options.detail: Also spelled -d. A named dir/ or . includes its immediate entries. A named dir without the slash adds just the directory. --recursive takes precedence. --files-from and --list-only imply --dirs unless disabled.

options.summary: List one directory with an older peer
options.detail: Also spelled --old-d. Emulates --dirs for a peer without that option using recursion and an exclusion for deeper entries.

options.summary: Create missing parents of the destination
options.detail: Normally only the last path component may be missing. End the destination in / to require a directory even for one source file. Use --relative when new parent directories should inherit source attributes.

options.summary: Keep each recursive scan on its starting filesystem
options.detail: Also spelled -x. Each explicitly named source starts its own scan. By default a crossed mount point appears as an empty directory. Repeat -x to omit it entirely. A bind mount of the same device counts as the same filesystem. The restriction also applies during deletion.

options.summary: Update only paths already at the destination
options.detail: Also spelled --ignore-non-existing. Skips creation of files and directories. Combining it with --ignore-existing suppresses all file updates but still permits deletions. This transfer rule leaves the sender's file list intact.

options.summary: Remove sender files after successful duplication
options.detail: Directories remain. Use only completed files. Rsync skips removal if the source size or modification time changes during transfer. For a local copy, versions 3.2.6 and newer also guard against removing the receiver's copy of the same path.

options.summary: Omit empty directory chains from the file list
options.detail: Also spelled -m. Pruning operates on the sender's file list after filtering and requires a complete scan. A size-based transfer rule still leaves its file in that list. Protect directories with explicit filter rules if deletions are enabled.

options.summary: Disable copying directory entries without recursion
options.detail: Also spelled --no-d. Use after --dirs or with --files-from to override its directory-entry default. Recursive descent is controlled separately by -r.

options.summary: Omit leading source path components
options.detail: Also spelled --no-R. Overrides -R, including the default from --files-from. Relative paths inside a recursively copied tree still retain their hierarchy.

options.summary: Transfer attributes of intermediate directories
options.detail: Also spelled --i-d. Restores the usual --relative behavior after --no-implied-dirs. Implied path components are sent as directories even if the sender reached them through symlinks.

options.summary: Allow traversal across filesystem boundaries
options.detail: Also spelled --no-x. Clears earlier -x settings. Only directories reached by the selected traversal participate.

options.summary: Keep empty directory chains in the file list
options.detail: Also spelled --no-m. Reverses -m. Filter and recursion rules still control which directories enter the list.

options.summary: Use line endings in input lists again
options.detail: Reverses -0 for --files-from, include/exclude lists and merged filter files. Embedded newlines then separate records.

options.summary: Copy the targets of source symlinks

options.summary: Follow source symlinks to directories
options.detail: Also spelled -k. The sender treats directory links as real directories. Links to ordinary files keep their usual treatment. A trailing slash on an explicit directory-link operand can follow just that link.

options.summary: Keep destination symlinks to matching directories
options.detail: Also spelled -K. When the sender supplies a real directory, the receiver writes its contents through an existing directory symlink. Normally the receiver replaces that link with a directory. Use only with trusted destination links.

options.summary: Skip copying symlinks as symlinks
options.detail: Also spelled --no-l. Use after -a to disable its implied -l. Options such as --copy-links can still copy the referent.

options.summary: Restore ownership checks on symlink path components
options.detail: Upstream 3.5.2 supports this option. Both reviewed Ubuntu releases reject it. Clears --insecure-links for paths supplied by the operator. This is separate from the treatment of symlinks in the transferred tree.

options.summary: Turn off symlink target munging
options.detail: Overrides a previous --munge-links on the affected side. The other side can have its own policy.

options.summary: Select the transfer compression algorithm
options.detail: Also spelled --zc. Overrides normal negotiation and enables compression unless the choice is none. Use rsync --version for compiled choices such as zstd, lz4, zlibx or zlib. The remote peer must support the chosen method.

forms.grammar: Zlib and zlibx support levels 1 to 9, default 6. Zstd supports -131072 to 22, default 3. Lz4 has no tunable level.

special_values.meaning: Choose default 6 with zlib or zlibx
Disable zlib or zlibx, choose default 3 for zstd, or use the only lz4 level

variants.ordering: Higher supported levels generally trade speed for compression. Values outside algorithm limits are clamped.

options.summary: Set the compression level for the chosen algorithm
options.detail: Also spelled --zl. For zlib or zlibx use 1 to 9, -1 for default 6, or 0 for off. For zstd use -131072 to 22, with 0 selecting default 3. Lz4 has no configurable level. Limits are clamped. Pair with --compress-choice for a predictable interpretation.

forms.grammar: Positive counts request workers only for thread-enabled zstd. Negative counts become zero. An upstream 3.5.2 daemon sender caps requests at eight workers.

special_values.meaning: Use the rsync thread for compression

when_absent.meaning: Compress in the rsync thread

options.summary: Set the number of sender compression workers
options.detail: Also spelled --zt. Upstream 3.5.2 supports this option. Both reviewed Ubuntu releases reject it. One or more workers require enabled zstd compression and a thread-capable libzstd. Other algorithms ignore the setting. The receiver's decompression is unaffected. A daemon sender caps the request at eight workers.

variants.meaning: Filename suffixes for legacy compression exceptions

forms.grammar: Use suffixes without a leading dot. An empty string clears the list. The reviewed compressors ignore per-file changes.

when_absent.meaning: Use the compiled skip list where the compressor supports it

options.summary: Set the legacy list of compression exceptions
options.detail: Takes suffixes separated by /, for example gz/jpg/zip. None of the compression methods in the reviewed releases supports changing the level per file, so this setting has no effect.

options.summary: Select classic zlib compression
options.detail: Compatibility spelling for --compress-choice=zlib. Use --compress-choice to name other algorithms explicitly.

options.summary: Select zlibx compression
options.detail: Compatibility spelling for --compress-choice=zlibx. This selects a specific algorithm even on peers offering newer methods.

options.summary: Clear the selected compression method
options.detail: Also spelled --no-z. Cancels -z and the explicit algorithm choice. A separate --compress-level can still request compression.

options.summary: Choose the daemon configuration file
options.detail: Daemon startup normally reads /etc/rsyncd.conf. An unprivileged daemon started over a remote shell defaults to rsyncd.conf in its working directory.

options.summary: Start an rsync daemon
options.detail: Starts the server that exports modules from rsyncd.conf. A client connects using host::module or rsync://host/module without adding --daemon. Socket-activated startup uses the supplied connection.

options.summary: Override a global daemon configuration parameter
options.detail: With --daemon, -M sets a configuration parameter. Supply NAME=VALUE as one argument. The daemon applies it after the global settings and before the first module. In client mode -M instead passes an option to the remote rsync.

options.summary: Run the standalone daemon in the background
options.detail: Restores default detachment after --no-detach. A daemon invoked over an existing inetd or sshd connection stays attached to that connection.

options.summary: Keep the standalone daemon in the foreground
options.detail: Use under a service supervisor or debugger. With an existing inetd or sshd connection this switch has no effect.

categories.description: Retain partial transfers and backup copies.
categories.name: Recovery

options.detail: Normally rsync removes the unfinished temporary file. --partial can leave the incomplete file at its final name, replacing an older destination. Use --partial-dir to keep it separately for the next delta transfer.
options.summary: Retain unfinished file data for a retry

options.detail: Also spelled -b. Files about to be overwritten or deleted are backed up. By default backups stay alongside the originals with a ~ suffix. Without --backup-dir, directory times are omitted. With --delete, a trailing protect rule for the suffix is added unless --delete-excluded is set. An earlier filter rule can take precedence.
options.summary: Keep prior destination files as backups

forms.grammar: Literal text appended to the backed-up filename.

when_absent.meaning: Use ~ without --backup-dir and an empty suffix with --backup-dir

options.summary: Choose the ending added to backup names
options.detail: With --backup the normal suffix is ~. With --backup-dir it defaults to empty. Supply the exact ending, including any desired leading dot.

options.summary: Write updates directly into the destination file
options.detail: Other hard links see changes immediately. Readers can see incomplete data, and interruption leaves the file partially updated. Implies --partial and conflicts with --partial-dir and --delay-updates. The receiver needs write permission on the file.

options.summary: Append the missing tail of a growing file
options.detail: Only use when the shorter receiver file is a known identical prefix. Existing bytes are not verified. Equal or longer receiver files are skipped. Writes happen in place, so an interruption leaves a shorter partially updated file.

options.summary: Append to a growing file and verify the full result
options.detail: Checks existing receiver bytes as well as the appended tail. Still skips equal or longer recipient files and writes in place. An interrupted run can leave an incomplete file. For protocol versions older than 30, either append switch uses this verification.

options.summary: Store zero-filled regions as holes
options.detail: Also spelled -S. Saves disk blocks only on a destination filesystem supporting sparse files. With --inplace or --preallocate, whether holes are created also depends on the kernel, filesystem and transfer mode.

options.summary: Reserve space before writing destination files
options.detail: Requires filesystem-level preallocation support on the receiver. Allocation can reduce fragmentation but may slow the copy. Sparse holes in preallocated files also depend on kernel and filesystem support.

variants.meaning: Directory for retained partial file data

bare.reason: This is a text/selector grammar, not an unsuffixed scalar measurement

forms.grammar: A relative directory is resolved beside each receiving file. An absolute path shares one directory.

when_absent.meaning: Use RSYNC_PARTIAL_DIR with --partial if set, or normal partial-file handling

options.summary: Keep incomplete data in a separate directory
options.detail: Implies --partial. A relative name creates a holding directory beside each destination file. A later delta transfer can reuse it while the original destination remains in place. Whole-file mode discards partial basis files. Keep the directory private from other writers.

options.summary: Install completed files near the end of the transfer
options.detail: The receiver holds updated files in .~tmp~ or --partial-dir, then renames them in succession. The switch requires a full file list and space for the extra copies. The set of renames is not atomic. Incompatible with --inplace and append mode.

options.summary: Install new and changed symlinks after regular files
options.detail: Upstream 3.5.2 supports this option. Both reviewed Ubuntu releases reject it. The receiver must support this switch. An interruption before installation leaves old link targets in place and new links missing. Use --delete-delay or --delete-after to keep old targets until late. Needs the complete list and conflicts with -H, --remove-source-files and alternate basis directories.

forms.grammar: Path on the receiver for temporary file data.

when_absent.meaning: Normally create temporary output beside its destination

options.summary: Choose scratch space for incoming files
options.detail: Also spelled -T. The default is the destination file's directory. With a scratch directory on another filesystem the receiver must copy the result over the destination instead of renaming it, exposing a partial update during the final copy. At daemon startup this sets the default scratch directory. A module's temp dir setting takes precedence.

options.summary: Show progress and keep partial files
options.detail: Combines --partial and --progress. The incomplete file can remain at the final path after interruption. Use a separate --partial-dir when an older destination must remain usable.

options.summary: Flush each finished file to storage
options.detail: The receiving process calls fsync for each completed file. This adds write latency and can slow the transfer.

options.summary: Write zero-filled regions normally
options.detail: Also spelled --no-S. Clears -S. Disk allocation can still depend on the receiving filesystem.

options.summary: Clear the request to update files in place
options.detail: Normally the receiver writes a temporary file and renames it on completion. --append, --append-verify or --write-devices can still imply in-place updates.

options.summary: Clear both append transfer modes
options.detail: Disables --append and --append-verify. A separately requested --inplace remains in effect.

options.summary: Clear the request to retain unfinished files
options.detail: Cancels --partial or that part of -P. A partial directory can still retain data, and an in-place write has already changed the destination.

options.summary: Install completed file updates individually
options.detail: Clears --delay-updates. Each completed temporary file can then be renamed into place without waiting for the final update pass.

options.summary: Clear delayed symlink installation
options.detail: Upstream 3.5.2 supports this option. Both reviewed Ubuntu releases reject it. Reverses --delay-symlinks so symlink updates can proceed during the transfer.

options.summary: Clear the request for backup copies
options.detail: Cancels -b. A specified --backup-dir still implies backups.
Implies --backup. Relative paths start at the destination directory. Backups keep their original names unless --suffix is set. A receiving daemon confines backups to its module.

forms.grammar: Directory path used with backup behavior for replaced/deleted destination files; relative paths resolve according to rsync's documented destination rules.

when_absent.meaning: Use the normal backup location/naming rules when backups are enabled.
